generator.program.note: The joint-firs' own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: jointed green switch stems with whorled branchlets.

growth.note: A joint-fir is grown to ten years; its clump is full well before.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

appearance.note: Grey-green, glaucous switch stems, the branchlets on narrow leaf cards, until a species states its own.

traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Gymnosperms (DELTA, 2008 onwards, version of 5 August 2019), Ephedraceae: mostly shrubby switch plants, often rhizomatous, a few vines or small trees, that photosynthesise with their grooved, jointed green stems; the leaves are reduced to small single-veined scales soon shed, opposite or in whorls, usually of three; nearly always dioecious.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 159, 160, 161, family Ephedraceae: rhizome habit long_creeping (underground stems), often; read as {"long_creeping": "often"}.
